clue.text: Smart Alec's old way to get a port

parts.note: wise is an archaic noun for way or manner, as in 'in no wise'
Acre is a historic port in northern Israel

explanation.surface: A know-all brags of an old route he took to reach a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Smart Alec's' reads as 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A wiseacre is a person who affects great wisdom, the same know-all type as a smart alec: a synonym.

clue.text: Thin girl whose will is so elusive?

definitions.meaning: a slight, slender girl is described as a mere ... of a girl
the will-o'-the-... is the elusive marsh light, so this is the thing whose 'will' goes with it

explanation.surface: A slender young woman whose resolve keeps slipping away.
explanation.definitionFit: A wisp is a slight slender person, and the phantom light will-o'-the-wisp is proverbially elusive.

clue.text: Filming art centre where discharge follows training

parts.note: making a film is shooting it
a gallery is a place where art is displayed

explanation.surface: A film crew at an arts venue where someone is dismissed after a course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharge' suggests dismissal after training, but it is a gun fired after it is trained on a target.
explanation.definitionFit: At a shooting range people train their guns on targets and then fire, a cryptic description of the venue.

clue.text: Interview posh woman representing clubs in lawsuit

indicators.note: one set of letters stands for, or takes the place of, another inside the lawsuit word

parts.note: an action is a legal case brought in court
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
Di is a woman's name, short for Diana

explanation.surface: A grand lady is questioned about a golfing case before the courts.
explanation.definitionFit: An audition is a trial interview for a performer seeking a part, a close synonym in that sense.

clue.text: Right house to accommodate favoured ungulate

indicators.note: to accommodate is to take in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: in favour, popular, is in

explanation.surface: The correct building is chosen to house a popular hoofed animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhinoceros is a hoofed mammal, an example of an ungulate.

clue.text: Stink over Greek character's first. bakery product

indicators.note: the Greek letter is told to come first, ahead of the other piece

parts.note: mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: over in an across clue means the word is turned round, read from right to left

parts.note: niff is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: A bad smell before a Greek's letter comes out of the bakery.
explanation.definitionFit: A muffin is a small baked bread or cake sold by bakers: an example.

clue.text: Not carried, reportedly, or delivered!

parts.note: a baby still in the womb is not yet born; 'not borne' (not carried) sounds the same, and it has not been delivered either

explanation.surface: Something reported as not having been brought along or handed over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Borne' means carried; said aloud, 'not borne' is the same as the word for a baby not yet delivered.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby not yet delivered is still to be born, which fits both readings of the clue.

clue.text: Permanently benefit when head intervenes? Really!

indicators.note: the headland word comes in between the other two pieces

parts.note: for good means for ever, permanently
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness place names
for the sake of someone is for their benefit

explanation.surface: A permanent benefit arises when a manager steps in.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation of exasperation means much the same as 'Really!': an idiom.

clue.text: What a hole — but the drink flows here!

definitions.text: What a hole — but the drink flows here!

parts.words: What a hole — but the drink flows here
parts.note: golfers call the clubhouse bar the hole after the eighteenth, where drinks are served

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a dump of a place, though at least there is plenty of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What a hole' sounds like a complaint, but it describes a golf hole number that is really the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf has eighteen holes, so the next 'hole' is the clubhouse bar, a jocular golfing idiom.

clue.text: Closure of shelter in southern county

indicators.note: the shelter word sits inside the other letters

parts.note: Down is a county of Northern Ireland
a hut is a simple shelter

explanation.surface: The closing of a refuge somewhere in the south of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A shutdown is the closing of a factory or system, a synonym for closure.

clue.text: Out East, insisted course must include fine seafood

indicators.note: out tells us to take a letter out of the word for insisted

parts.note: swore, as in swore blind, means insisted

indicators.note: the course word has to contain the other letter

parts.note: a dish is a course of a meal
F stands for fine, as on pencil leads

explanation.surface: Someone abroad in the East demands that the menu include good fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' deletes E from SWORE to leave SWOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Swordfish is a large fish eaten as a steak: an example of seafood.

clue.text: Noble piece of music being broadcast

parts.note: a bar is a short measured section of music
a programme that is being transmitted is on

explanation.surface: An aristocratic piece of music going out on air.
explanation.definitionFit: A baron is a member of the lowest rank of the peerage, so a noble: an example.

clue.text: Way English teachers initially let it stand

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of teachers is used

explanation.surface: English teachers decide on a way to leave something unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Stet is the proofreading instruction meaning let the original wording stand: Latin for 'let it stand'.

clue.text: Ring son in 24, being farthest from centre

parts.note: on an archery or rifle target the outer is the ring furthest from the bull

indicators.note: the son letter goes inside the test word

parts.note: the answer to 24 across is test, and an MOT is the British annual roadworthiness test for vehicles

explanation.surface: A ring and a son at a test match, as far as possible from the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: '24' points to the answer to 24 across (TEST), to be replaced by a synonym, MOT, the UK's yearly vehicle safety test.
explanation.definitionFit: Outermost means positioned furthest out, the farthest from the centre: a synonym.

clue.text: Lacking will to cross river between parts of Us

indicators.note: one piece goes across, or through, the other

parts.note: someone who dies without a will dies intestate

explanation.surface: Someone dying without a will crosses a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Us' looks like the pronoun but is the US, the United States, whose parts are states.
explanation.definitionFit: Interstate means between or involving different states of the US, as in an interstate highway.

clue.text: Wally's given no work, accepting reduced pay quietly

indicators.note: the word no takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: reduced means the last letter of the pay word is cut off

parts.note: income is what one is paid
p (piano) is the musical direction for quietly
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A fool is given no job and has to take a pay cut without complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: Wally is British slang for a fool; the 's reads as 'is'. 'Reduced' turns INCOME into INCOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Wally is British slang for a silly person, the same meaning as a fool or idiot: a synonym.

clue.text: Goin' to pieces, say, seeing metal cup

indicators.note: say tells us to speak the phrase and listen to how it sounds

parts.note: going to pieces is panicking, here with the dropped g of casual speech

explanation.surface: Someone falling apart at the sight of a tin mug.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'Goin'' signals the dropped G of 'panickin'', which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pannikin is a small metal drinking cup or pan: a synonym.

clue.text: Tool found in dead zebra

indicators.note: the letters are found in the run of the next two words

explanation.surface: An implement discovered inside a dead zebra.
explanation.definitionFit: An adze is a cutting tool like an axe with its blade at right angles to the handle: an example.

clue.text: They fear being shot like birds

indicators.note: being shot means knocked about, broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Creatures afraid of the guns, like game birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Feathery means covered in or resembling feathers, as birds are.

clue.text: Experience a French duke avoided for this reason

indicators.note: avoided means these letters are left out of the experience word

parts.note: to undergo something is to experience it
un is the French for a

explanation.surface: A French aristocrat sidesteps an ordeal for a reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergo is Latin for therefore, meaning for this reason: a synonym.

clue.text: A versatile athlete may be, whatever happens

definitions.meaning: an all-rounder could compete in any of the events of a meeting
an idiom meaning regardless, come what may

explanation.surface: An all-round sportsman will compete regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means regardless or whatever happens, and literally an all-rounder can compete in any race.

clue.text: Confidence in myself, entering exam

indicators.note: the exam word goes into the word for myself

parts.note: me is the pronoun for oneself
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: Feeling self-assured on going into a test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link; 'entering' places ORAL in ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Morale is a group's or person's confidence and spirits: a synonym.

clue.text: Thus desire to keep everyone rather anaemic

indicators.note: to keep is to hold, so the first pair holds the other

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
all means everyone
a wish is a desire

explanation.surface: Accordingly wanting to keep everyone close, though looking pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Sallowish means somewhat sallow, a sickly yellowish pallor that suggests anaemia.

clue.text: Hard old boy leaves musician in lift

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so these letters go out of the musician word

parts.note: an oboist plays the oboe
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A tough former pupil walks out on a musician in a lift.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoist is a lift, a device for raising loads: a synonym.

clue.text: Analyse flowing water in Hampshire

definitions.meaning: to analyse a substance is to put it to the ...
a chalk stream river in Hampshire, a southern English county

explanation.surface: Examining the river water in a southern English county.
explanation.definitionFit: To test is to analyse, and the Test is a famous trout river in Hampshire.

clue.text: Flood defence a king viewed in colour

indicators.note: the king letter is seen inside the colour word

parts.note: dye gives colour
K is the abbreviation for king, in chess and cards

explanation.surface: A monarch inspected in colour at a sea barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A dyke is an embankment built to keep out floods: a synonym.

clue.text: Where gladiatorial contests took place a long time back

indicators.note: back tells us the whole phrase is read backwards

parts.note: an is the form of the article a used before a vowel
an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Gladiators fought there in an age long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like part of the time phrase meaning long ago, but it is the reversal signal; 'a' must be read as its other form, the one used before vowels.
explanation.definitionFit: The arena was the sanded central area of a Roman amphitheatre where gladiators fought.

clue.text: A nicety I originally respected freely in travelling

indicators.note: freely means loosely, without fixed order, so the letters are rearranged
originally means only the first letter of respected is used

explanation.surface: A fine point was respected without fuss while on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Itineracy is the state of travelling from place to place, a variant of itinerancy.

clue.text: Palace serving two dioceses

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and diocese in Cambridgeshire
a see is a bishop's diocese

explanation.surface: A palace that serves two church districts.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elysee Palace in Paris is the official residence of the French president: an example.

clue.text: Gas is extremely explosive, choking your old man

indicators.note: choking means holding tight round the neck, so the outer letters wrap the others
extremely means take the extreme, first and last letters of explosive

parts.note: thy is the old form of your
Len is a man's name

explanation.surface: A dangerously explosive gas is throttling your father.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethylene is a flammable hydrocarbon gas used in making plastics: an example.
